title.narrative: Emergency Assistance for Rehabilitation and Reconstruction

description.narrative: In line with the Master Plan for Recovery and Reconstruction for Central Sulawesi (the Master Plan), the Emergency Assistance for Rehabilitation and Reconstruction (EARR) will support the Government of Indonesia in building back better critical infrastructure damaged by the devastating disasters in Central Sulawesi Province in September 2018, where a 7.4-magnitude earthquake triggered a near-field tsunami, landslides, and major liquefaction.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Access for affected people, including women and children, to resilient and inclusive infrastructure restored

At least 200,000 individuals have access to infrastructure that is resilient, inclusive, and operational Achievement: 867724 Progress/Status: By end Sep 2024, a total of 667,724 individuals have access to infrastructure that is resilient, inclusive, and operational
Achievement by rehabilitated and reconstructed seaport infrastructure that could accessed by at least 200,000 individuals is resilient, inclusive and operational. Data Source: Periodic progress reports prepared by the executing agencies
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Airport rehabilitated and reconstructed Indicator: One airport rehabilitated and/or reconstructed to disaster-resilient standards and with gender-responsive and inclusive features Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Completed.
Reconstruction of Runway (CW Airport 1) The contractor was mobilized from 30 September 2021. The construction was completed on 23 May 2023.
Reconstruction of Terminal Building (CW Airport 2) The contractor was mobilized from 7 December 2021. The construction was completed on 31 August 2023. Data Source: Periodic progress report prepared by Ministry of Transportation

Output: Human settlement infrastructure constructed, rehabilitated, and upgraded Indicator: At least one educational institution reconstructed to disaster-resilient standards and with gender-responsive and inclusive features Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Reconstruction of Islamic Institute (IAIN):
The contract signed in December 2020. Completed with construction progress reached 100% in December 2022.
Gender-responsive and inclusive features include: separate male and female restrooms, accessible door handles, and a lactation room. Safety measures, including non-slip floors, ramps, and emergency lights, were also added to ensure safe evacuation for everyone, including people with disabilities. Data Source: Periodic progress report prepared by the Ministry of Public Works and Housing and local governments

Output: Human settlement infrastructure constructed, rehabilitated, and upgraded Indicator: Potable water supply services provided to serve 14,510 households (benefitting at least 27,000 women and girls), including at least 6,100 household service connections installed and established with prior consultation (45% participation of women in consultations) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: PASIGALA Water Treatment and Distribution (WTD) Subproject.
As many as 16,486 households (benefitting 30,870 women and girls) are served with potable water provided by the system constructed through the project (water treatment plant and distribution lines). It includes 9,053 new HSCs installed by the project and 2,525 newly installed HSCs by the World Bank's funded project (CSSRP). The remaining 4,908 are existing HSCs connected and served by the project.
Participation of women is on-track. Out of 20,413 participants, 10,785 (53%) were women.

Output: Ports rehabilitated and reconstructed Indicator: Three ports rehabilitated to disaster-resilient standards and with gender-responsive and inclusive features Achievement: 2 Progress/Status: Completed.
